sections.label: Stamp duty on electronic records
sections.summary: The Stamp Duties Act will be amended to levy stamp duty on electronic records transferring interest in immovable properties and shares.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: First, in line with our Smart Nation efforts, the Stamp Duties Act will be amended to provide for stamp duty to be levied on electronic records that effect a transfer of interest in immovable properties and shares.

sections.label: Recovering interest on stamp duty remission
sections.summary: The Act will provide that the Minister can recover interest from a taxpayer who fails to comply with remission conditions for upfront stamp duty remission.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The second change is to provide in the Act that the Minister can recover interest from a taxpayer who fails to comply with the remission conditions, in respect of upfront stamp duty remission that had been granted to him.

sections.label: Amendments to corporate restructuring relief
sections.summary: Amendments will be made to section 15 of the Act, which provides stamp duty relief for corporate restructuring with no substantial change in beneficial interest.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Third, we will make amendments to section 15 of the Act, which provides relief from stamp duty for corporate restructuring where there is no substantial change in beneficial interest of the transferred assets.

sections.label: Stamp duty share of taxes
sections.summary: Last year, stamp duty comprised some 7% of all taxes collected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Last year, stamp duty comprised some 7% of all taxes collected.

sections.label: Regulatory stance on proptech blockchain startups
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to clarify the Government's regulatory stance towards proptech startups using blockchain to decentralise electronic records of property transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify the Government’s regulatory stance towards “proptech” startups that use blockchain to decentralise the electronic records of property transactions?

sections.label: Plans on electronic records security awareness
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government plans to go beyond these measures to promote awareness of and address concerns about security and reliability of electronic records for real estate transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Does the Government have plans to go beyond these measures to promote awareness of and address concerns about the security and reliability of using electronic records to execute real estate transactions?

sections.label: Legal clarity for new technologies
sections.summary: Businesses and consumers would benefit from greater legal clarity and certainty over new technologies, and Government agencies are studying the legislative framework for electronic transactions and digitalising property transaction processes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Businesses and consumers would, indeed, benefit from greater legal clarity and certainty over such new technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And that is why Government agencies are separately studying the legislative framework for electronic transactions in Singapore as well as how best to streamline and digitalise property transaction processes.

sections.label: Review of Electronic Transactions Act
sections.summary: The Ministry of Communications and Information and the Infocomm Media Development Authority are currently reviewing the ETA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Ministry of Communications and Information  and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) are currently reviewing the ETA.

sections.label: Feasibility of electronic property transactions
sections.summary: The workgroup aims to look into the feasibility of enabling property transactions to be conducted electronically from start to finish in a secure and verifiable way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The aim of the workgroup is to look into the feasibility of enabling property transactions to be conducted electronically from start to finish, but, importantly, to do so in a secure and verifiable way.
